name: Refugee/Asylum Status (CONARE)

qualifying_event.description: A person unable to return to their home country due to a well-founded fear of persecution may apply for refugee status; applications are received by the National Office for Refugees (ONR) and decided by the National Commission for Refugees (CONARE).
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Written testimony explaining the inability to return; supporting evidence (photos, certificates, reports); passport or sworn declaration if unavailable.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicants must be physically present in the Dominican Republic and apply within 15 days of arrival.
Requires written testimony explaining the inability to return home, plus any supporting evidence, six passport photos, and a medical certificate regarding infectious diseases.

outcome.duration_length: Renewable 30-day evidence document while pending; final status duration not specified in source

sources.title: UNHCR Dominican Republic -- How to request asylum: 15-day filing window, ONR intake, CONARE decision, 30-day renewable evidence document, explicit bar on paid work while pending

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Dominican Republic). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to UNHCR (tier 2), not a primary Dominican government page; no official CONARE or ONR government page was located and fetchable during this research pass (a Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores transparency page for the Comisión Nacional Para Refugiados exists at mirex.gob.do/transparencia/comision-nacional-para-refugiados/ but was not fetched for substantive process detail in this pass). The explicit bar on paid work while an application is pending is a real, stated restriction worth flagging -- applicants can be in status limbo for extended periods without any lawful income. study_rights, family_can_join, and leads_to_pr/leads_to_citizenship are NOT stated in the source and are set to the schema's most conservative values (none/false) as a placeholder rather than a confirmed fact -- flagged explicitly since the schema does not allow null here. The 15-day filing deadline from arrival is notably strict compared to other countries in this dataset. This file is unrelated to the jus-soli statelessness issue discussed in do_citizenship_by_descent.json's notes -- that is a nationality/civil-registry problem for people born in DR, not an asylum/refugee process for people arriving from elsewhere.
